summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyo Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a graduate research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2014) and served there as a publicly recruited researcher in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University circa 1980–1989 and held a post there circa 1998.
Yun Ji specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ji earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University by 2006 and served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Yungfen Ma works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed a PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).
Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951 and held a post there from circa 1952 to 2014.

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, VTSIOM (~1988–2003), and the Levada Center (~2003–2006).
Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University circa 1937–1941 and served as a professor there circa 1961–1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chizan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, holding posts at Koyasan University (1954, 1965–1967), Nagoya University (1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin (1987), and Shuchiin University (2001).

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After graduate studies at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami, Wakahara held teaching posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1999 as assistant professor, 2011–2013 as professor).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University (~1968–2005), where he became emeritus professor.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate from Kyushu University, later serving at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1961–1974), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2004).

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, and Hidenaka Tanaka. He taught at Kyoto, Tokai, Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka Universities.

Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Kawasaki studied under Seio Okuda and held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Louis Renou, Atsuuji Ashikaga, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard, holding posts at Kyoto University (1957–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1972–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hitotsubashi (1983–2018), Kyoto University (~2006–2019), Center for Peace and Reconciliation (2008), and Center of the Tokyo Raids (2019).

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1969), earned a doctorate from Rissho University (1990), and held assistant professor posts at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).
